tree_state: docs/procedures/nat-064/ and docs/procedures/nat-063/ERRATA.md are uncommitted at recording time and are committed in the commit that follows this record; the recorded commit is its parent
summary: Source review of how rd=md0 reaches PID 1 in the payload kernel (IOFindBSDRoot -> mdevadd from /chosen/memory-map RAMDisk -> vfs_mountroot/mockfs -> load_init_program -> init exit panic), a host rebuild comparison of the payload with the pinned mkpayload.py, and the explanation of the !BSD line of NAT-063. Findings: (1) !BSD is the project's own 100 ms wait for rd=md*, not a 30 s timeout (the task premise was wrong); measured about 102.5 ms of kernel time after correcting the 1.024 microsecond-field inflation, which shows a deadline wake worked; (2) the NAT-063 panic is the missing RAMDisk property; (3) mkpayload.py --ramdisk adds one segment and one 52-byte ADT property, the rebuild of the existing payload is byte-equal and reproducible, and with a ramdisk adt_size becomes 14008 (a multiple of 8) so the NAT-062 adt_size header fix must not be carried over; (4) the loader's RAMDisk rebase code exists but has never executed on the phone; (5) the NAT-063 README's 1.7 s kernel interval is a host receive-time gap (errata added). A minimal NAT-065 design (probe init that exits with a status so the run ends in a panic that carries a verdict) with host tests, mutants and decision-file items is specified. No hardware claim; nothing ran on the phone.
evidence_category: source-review of pinned XNU 22.5.0 originals plus project patches and the NAT-052 loader tree, and a host-test (payload rebuild/compare); not a measurement of the S24. The 102.5 ms figure is derived from the NAT-063 native-device log stamps and the cited rtclock code.
